name: S-Class Time Warden
body:
S-class time wardens can reach into both the past and future, drawing them into the present with equal ease and shaping them to meet her needs. They manipulate chronal dissonance, turning it back on itself or unleashing it against their enemies in controlled bursts of power.

Role: Time wardens are spellcasters akin to bards. They practice chronothurgy, which allows them to look through the infinite timelines and choose one in which they get the most benefit for the effect they hope to create.

Note: The s-class time warden is an alternate, superior version of the time warden class. They retain all of the standard time warden progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select time warden archetypes without specific adjustments.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8.

Starting Wealth: 3d6 × 10 gp (average 105 gp.) In addition, an s-class time warden begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The s-class time warden’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (all), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Survival (Wis), Swim (Str), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class time warden.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

S-class time wardens are proficient with all simple weapons. They are not proficient with any armor or shields.

Chronothurgy (Sp)

A time warden casts temporal spells drawn from the time warden spell list. She can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time. Because of their alien nature compared to most magic, chronothurgy spells are more difficult to duplicate or turn into magic items. When using other spells to duplicate the effect of chronothurgy spells (such as limited wish, wish, or miracle), or when using spells to price magic items based on chronothurgy, treat the spell level as if it was 50% higher (minimum +1 level). Thus, for these purposes, a 4th-level chronothurgy spell is treated as being 6th level, and a 6th-level chronothurgy spell is treated as being 9th level.

To learn or cast a chronothurgy spell, a time warden must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a time warden’s spell is: 10 + the spell level + the time warden’s Charisma modifier

Like other spellcasters, a time warden can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Her base daily spell allotment is given on Table: S-Class Time Warden. In addition, she receives bonus spells per day if she has a high Charisma score.

The time warden’s selection of spells is extremely limited.

A time warden begins play knowing four 0-level spells and two 1st-level spells of the time warden’s choice. At each new time warden level, she gains one or more new spells, as indicated on Table: Time Warden Spells Known. (Unlike spells per day, the number of spells a time warden knows is not affected by her Charisma score. The numbers on Table: Time Warden Spells Known are fixed.)

Upon reaching 3rd level, and at every other time warden level after that (5th, 7th, and so on), a time warden can choose to learn a new spell in place of one she already knows. In effect, the time warden “loses” the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least one level lower than the highest-level time warden spell the time warden can cast.

A time warden can swap only a single spell at any given level and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that she gains new spells known for the level. A time warden need not prepare her spells in advance. She can cast any spell she knows at any time, assuming she has not yet used up her allotment of spells per day for the spell’s level.

Motes of Time (Su)

Every s-class time warden begins play with a pool of temporal energy generated by their past and future selves from which the time warden draws motes of time. An s-class time warden can draw a number of motes from her temporal pool each day equal to 3 + her time warden level. Regardless of the action taken or the number of motes spent, an s-class time warden can only spend motes of time once per round. By spending 1 mote of time as a free action, the time warden can use one of the following mote powers, as shown on Table: S-Class Time warden. Unless stated otherwise, she must gain the benefit before the start of her next turn.

Spare Second (1st): Take a swift action that does not count against the time warden’s normal limit of one swift action per round.
Personal Timeline (8th): Alter her personal timeline to one in which she received different training. This requires 1 hour of uninterrupted meditation. At the end of this time, the time warden can remove skill ranks from one skill and add them to a different skill, or exchange one feat for another feat, or exchange one spell known for a different spell known. In all cases the selection must meet all normal restrictions. Any change made remains in effect for 24 hours. A time warden cannot have more than 1 total change per three class levels in effect at the same time. Any attempt to make additional changes to her timeline fail.
Personal Casting Time (11th): Cast a spell as a swift action if it could normally be cast with a standard action. The time warden cannot cast any other spell on the same round this ability is used.

Retrocast (14th): Expend one of her unused spell slots so that an ally spellcaster regains one they spent. If the spellcaster prepares spells, the same spell is prepared again in the regained spell slot.

In addition, the time warden can spend 1 mote of time to gain a +1d4 mote bonus to certain check results and effects, as shown on Table: S-Class Time warden. The mote bonus increases to +2d4 at 8th level, and +3d4 at 16th level. The time warden can decide to add this bonus immediately after seeing the result of the original die roll.

Defensive Retry (1st): One saving throw.
Detailed Retry (1st): One skill check or ability check.
Eldritch Retry (1st): One caster level check.
Ready for Anything (1st): Initiative.
Time of War (2nd): Armor class (as a dodge bonus) until the beginning of her next turn. Alternatively, the time warden can gain proficiency in a single weapon or type of armor for 24 hours.
Slow Spell (5th): Extend the duration of a time warden spell she has cast.
Sphere of Calm Time (17th): Grant any ally she can see her mote of time bonus to any one skill check or ability check that occurs entirely within 1 round.
Chronal Studies

At 3rd level, an s-class time warden becomes temporally bound to herself in an alternate timeline. This bond gives the time warden access to advanced practices, referred to as chronal studies. Chronal studies are specific packets of abilities that can’t be changed once the time warden starts down that specific path.

Standard time wardens can gain access to chronal studies as well, but when they do, their studies replace lord of time and the motes of time gained at 2nd, 8th, and 14th level. Chronal studies can be found at the end of this section.

Aevum (Sp or Su)

At 5th level, an s-class time warden selects a single aevum that she can use once per day plus one additional time at 6th level and every 3 time warden levels she attains beyond 6th. At each interval, the time warden also adds an additional aevum she can use instead. Spending an aevum is a standard action unless the ability’s description says otherwise. A sample list of aevum can be found at the end of this section for easy reference.

Lord of Time (Su)

At 20th level, each time the time warden regains the use of her spells and abilities for the day, she can also re-assign her skill points, feats, and spells known as she wishes.

She must meet the prerequisites for any new feats she selects, and she cannot change out a feat she is using as a prerequisite for other feats or abilities. The new selection of skill point allotment, feats, and spells known is instant, remaining (even in an antimagic field) until the time warden changes them again with this ability. Further, the time warden can add her Charisma modifier to her caster level when resisting any chronothurgy effect attempting to dispel her spells and abilities (such as the dispel duration spell or enforce dissonance aevum ability).

Favored Class Bonuses

Instead of receiving an additional skill rank or hit point whenever they gain a level in a favored class, some ancestries have the option of choosing from a number of other bonuses, depending upon their favored classes.

The following options are available to the listed ancestry who have time warden as their favored class, and unless otherwise stated, the bonus applies each time you select the listed favored class reward.

Drakorin: 1/4 times per day, you can spend a mote of time to recharge and use your breath weapon as a standard action.
Dwarf: Add +1/6 to your mote bonus (max +1).
Elf: Add one spell known from the time warden spell list. This spell must be at least one level below the highest spell level the time warden can cast.
Gnome: Add one spell known from the time warden spell list. This spell must be at least one level below the highest spell level the time warden can cast.
God-Blooded: Gain 1/6 of an additional aevum. This counts as the Aevum Mastery feat.
Halfling: Gain 1/6 of the future vitality mote power. If you already have that power, you can gain 1/6 of the improved future vitality mote power instead.
Human: Choose one—You gain 1/2 of an additional mote of time; or you gain 1/6 of a new mote power, which counts as the Mote Specialization feat.
Orc: Gain 1/6 of the Mote Mastery feat for the reaver or time thief.
Sample Aevum

The aevum presented here are available to all time wardens, not just s-class time wardens. For more aevum, please refer to the standard time warden source material.

Do Over (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 17th level.

As a swift action the time warden may spend 1 aevum to mark a moment as a restore point. All changes made during the next turn (damage dealt, resources spent, movement taken) should be noted by players and GM alike. At the beginning of the time warden’s next turn, before taking any other actions, she may spend two additional aevum as a full-round action to jump back in time to her restore point. This undoes everything that has happened in the past turn, since she marked a restore point. Creatures within 60 feet of the time warden remember the events of the now-erased round of action, while creatures further away are oblivious to the brief time jaunt.

Quadrus (Su)

By spending an aevum, multiple iterations of the time warden can exist in the same point in time for up to one minute per time warden level. This ability functions as mirror image, except it is a conjuration (summoning) effect with the shadow descriptor. The time warden adds a new image whenever she spends at least 1 mote of time within the duration, up to a maximum of 4 images. This effect does not automatically end when the time warden has 0 images remaining.

Altering Time

Every time warden is trained well enough that the changes she makes to her own or another creature’s timeline to gain her effects are subtle enough to cause no more disturbance than a wizard casting a time stop spell.

Shatter Time (Su)

By spending an aevum, the time warden can recharge her daily uses of motes. She regains a number of motes of time equal to 1d4 + her Charisma modifier. This cannot increase the number of motes available to above her daily mote total.

Swap (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 10th level.

The time warden may spend 1 aevum as a swift action to stop time and trade places with a creature within 60 feet before restoring the flow of time. The creature must be one the time warden could reach with the movement available to her at the time the power is used. The creature must also be one the time warden could lift and carry (neither too heavy for the time warden to move at all, nor grappled, entangled, or otherwise anchored in place).

If the time warden readies to use this power in response to an attack, she may make the Swap after the attack is announced, but before the roll is made. The attack cannot be aborted (because the time warden waits until it is already begun), and the attack roll is made against the new target.

A time warden of 10th level or higher may spend 2 aevum to use this ability as an immediate action (which normally functions as if the chronothurge has readied to use the power).

Temporal Feedback (Su)

By spending an aevum when adjacent to an ally who recently used a limited resource ability, the time warden can grant that ally the use of their ability back. If the ability is limited to uses per day (such as smite evil), the ally regains 1 use. If the ability is drawn from a pool (such as channel energy, ki, bardic performance, or rage), the ally regains a number of uses of that ability up to 1d4 + the time warden’s Charisma modifier. This cannot give the ally more uses of their ability than their maximum allowed.

Tenuous Existence (Su)

By spending an aevum, the time warden creates a tenuous link between her present and her immediate future self, calling that version of the time warden into her reality for 1 round per time warden level. This ability functions as project image, except as noted here. It is a conjuration (summoning) effect with the [shadow] descriptor and no saving throw. Damage dealt to either or both the time warden and her future self affects the time warden once (she makes only one saving throw when one is necessary), and any other positive or negative effects that would be applied to her future self are applied to the time warden instead. While using her future self’s senses, the time warden can interact with creatures and objects normally. When the effect ends or is dispelled, the time warden can choose to remain in her current space or the space occupied by her future self.

Chronal Studies
Ancient Past

Chronal studies into the ancient past bond the time warden to a version of themselves who lived centuries, or even millenia before their current timeperiod.

Instinctual Reflexes (Ex)

When she forms her bond at 3rd level, the time warden’s Reflex save progression becomes good. This equates to a +2 increase to her bonus at 3rd level, and follows the same path as her Will save bonus from there on.

Call Ancient Self (Sp)

Beginning at 7th level, the time warden automatically adds bear’s endurance and bull’s strength to her spells known as a summoner of her time warden level. She can cast each of those spells once per day as a spell-like ability, using herself as the only target, or twice per day at 20th level.

At 11th level, the time warden can also cast transformation as a spell-like ability once per day, or twice per day at 20th level.

Concurrent Evolution

Chronal studies into concurrent evolution bond the time warden to versions of themselves who evolved from many different things over eons given wildly different circumstances.

Unexpected Physiology (Ex)

When she forms her bond at 3rd level, the time warden gains a +1 natural armor bonus. This bonus increases by +1 at 7th level and every 4 levels thereafter, to a maximum of +5 at 19th level.

Call Concurrent Self (Sp)

Beginning at 7th level, the time warden adds all polymorph spells to her time warden spell list and gains Natural Spell as a feat, even if she doesn’t meet the prerequisites. She can learn polymorph spells at the lowest available level for any class, and using Natural Spell she retains her ability to cast spells in those forms. She also automatically adds monstrous physique I through IV to her spells known as a wizard of her time warden level when she gains access to spells of the appropriate level.

Once per day, the time warden can cast any transmutation spell she knows as a spell-like ability, using herself as the only target. She can do this twice per day at 20th level.

Far Future

Chronal studies into the far future bond the time warden to a version of themselves who lives centuries, or even millenia ahead of their current timeperiod.

Advances in Medicine (Ex)

When she forms her bond at 3rd level, the time warden’s Fortitude save progression becomes good. This equates to a +2 increase to her bonus at 3rd level, and follows the same path as her Will save bonus from there on.

Call Future Self (Sp)

Beginning at 7th level, the time warden automatically adds fox’s cunning and owl’s wisdom to her spells known as a summoner of her time warden level. She can cast each of those spells once per day as a spell-like ability, using herself 5 as the only target, or twice per day at 20th level.

Technological Paradox (Ex)

At 11th level, the time warden gains a non-consumable, technological weapon or armor worth up to 20,500 gp. She is proficient with that item, but its advanced status makes it worthless to anybody else in her current timeperiod. The value of the item can be increased to 60,000 gp at 15th level, and 220,000 gp at 20th level. At each interval, the time warden can either improve her item or select another as the previous item is pulled back to its proper timeline.

Traditionalists

Traditionalist studies include basic spellcasting improvement and a focus on magical precedent.

Bonus Feats

At 3rd level, and every odd level thereafter (5th, 7th, and so on), the time warden gains a bonus feat. At each such opportunity, she can choose a temporal feat, a metamagic feat, an item creation feat, or Spell Mastery. The time warden must still meet all prerequisites for a bonus feat, including caster level minimums.

Time Warden Multiclassing Options
Time Warden Variant Multiclass

A character who chooses time warden as her secondary class gains the following secondary class features.

Mote of Time: At 3rd level, she gains the mote of time class feature for a number of rounds per day equal to her Charisma modifier. She also gains up to 2 1st-level mote powers of her choice from the list presented here. She gains an additional 1st-level mote power at 7th, 15th, and 19th level.
Advanced Mote Power: At 7th level, she gains a 7th-level or lower mote power for which she meets the prerequisites as a time warden of her character level.
Cantrip: At 11th level, if she has a Charisma score of 10 or higher, she chooses a time warden cantrip and can cast that cantrip as a spell-like ability at will. She uses her character level as the caster level and Charisma as the cantrip’s key ability score.
Aevum: At 15th level, she gains one aevum for which the meets the prerequisites as a time warden of her character level.
Advanced Mote Power: At 19th level, she gains a 15th-level or lower mote power for which she meets the prerequisites as a time warden of her character level.
Dissonant Hero [Multiclass Feat]

Prerequisite(s): 5th-level time warden, at least 2 levels in non-time warden classes.

Benefit(s): Your time warden level counts as 2 higher when determining if you gain a new mote power or aevum, to a maximum of your character level. If you are an 11th-level or higher time warden, you can choose instead to gain lord of time when you reach 20th level.
